Writing & Ideas

The best workshops don't begin the day people walk into the room.

They begin long before that—with questions.

Questions about power, learning, leadership, belonging, democracy, and what becomes possible when people create space to think together.

This page is a collection of those questions.

Here you'll find essays, research, comics, talks, and practical resources that have shaped my work as a facilitator, researcher, and organizer. Some are grounded in scholarship. Others grew out of workshops, organizing campaigns, or conversations that stayed with me long after they ended.

I hope they spark new questions for you, too.

Start here #

If you're new to my work, these three pieces offer the best introduction to how I think.

Science is best communicated through identity and culture – how researchers are ensuring STEM serves their communities #

A comic adaptation of my research exploring how scientists from marginalized communities are reshaping science communication through identity, culture, and belonging.

Science Communication Spaces as "Pockets of Belonging" #

What if science communication wasn't simply about transmitting knowledge? Drawing on my research, this article explores how science communication spaces can become places where more people feel they belong—and why that matters for the future of science.

Science Communication Won't Save Us. Collective Action Will #

Science communication can help people understand the world—but understanding alone rarely changes it. In this essay, I explore what community organizing can teach us about moving from information to relationships, leadership, and collective action.

Science, Power & Belonging #

My scholarship explores how power, ideology, identity, and belonging shape science communication—and what science might become if it were more accountable to the communities it serves.

  • Science Communication Spaces as "Pockets of Belonging"

Learning, Facilitation & Creative Practice #

People don't become more collaborative by being told how.

They become more collaborative by practicing it together.

These writings explore participatory learning, improvisation, Theatre of the Oppressed, and designing meaningful workshop experiences.

Featured work

  • Using Theater to Uncover Youth Climate Change Narratives
  • The Landscape of Art-Science Collaboration Programs
  • Confronting Crises: Art-Science as Mirror, Connector, and Portal
  • Whimsy. Is there a role for laughter, subversive curve balls, ironic romance and “oh wow that’s cool” moments in the mainstreaming of knowledge and action in sustainability, climate change, and biodiversity?

Explore more facilitation →

Much of what I know about facilitation comes from organizing.

These essays explore what community organizing has taught me about leadership, power, strategy, relationships, and building collective capacity.
